subject: SLA & Liability: request for severity-indexed buyout and remedies
messages:
From: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@acme-med.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Medical Systems Procurement <procurement@acme-med.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA & Liability: request for severity-indexed buyout and remedies

Camila —

Thanks for the demo last week. Acme is very interested in Redwood for our inference tier, but procurement/legal flagged a number of concerns around SLA remedies. Given the safety-critical nature of our workload (medical device triggers), we need contractual levers beyond a monthly service credit. Specifically we propose the following: 

1) Severity-indexed buyout: an option for Acme to buy out the remainder of the contract (pro-rated) if we hit a Severity 1 incident (system unavailable for patient-impacting requests) that leads to missed regulated reporting or patient harm. Buyout should be available after 2 Severity 1 incidents within a 12-month period.

2) Fee-at-risk / liquidated damages: for Severity 1 and Severity 2 breaches, we want a pre-agreed fee schedule (not just credits) tied to committed fees (e.g., 3x monthly commit for Sev1, 1.5x for Sev2).

3) Latency guarantees: p95 inference latency <= 200ms for the provisioned dedicated pool; failure to meet p95 for 3 consecutive weeks should trigger fee-at-risk staging.

4) Auditability: daily uptime/latency telemetry exported to our Splunk instance (or a signed report) for the purposes of regulatory review.

We attached a redline (Acme_Redlines_SLA_20270110.pdf) with language. I know this is heavier than your standard T&Cs; please let us know what is feasible. We can set an executive call with legal/procurement later this week.

Appreciate a direct point of contact who can speak to contractual remedies and whether Redwood can accept a limited buyout and severity-indexed fee schedule.

—Elliot
Elliot Ross
Head of Procurement, Acme Medical Systems
procurement@acme-med.com
(415) 555-0198
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@acme-med.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA & Liability: request for severity-indexed buyout and remedies

Elliot —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I appreciate how specific you were about triggers and amounts; that helps. I want to be upfront that some of the asks (uncapped buyouts tied to safety events) are higher-risk than Redwood typically accepts, but I want to explore a pragmatic path forward.

I've looped in Chloe (legal) and Rishi (sales lead for enterprise medical accounts). Chloe — can you review the attached redline and the proposed severity schedule? Rishi — can we schedule an exec-level call for Thursday to align on risk tolerance and potential mitigations (e.g., escrow, capped buyout, on-call guarantees)?

Two quick questions for Acme:
- Can you confirm the contract term length and committed monthly spend you expect (so we can quantify fee-at-risk)?
- For telemetry, is a signed daily summary sufficient or do you require direct access to our metrics feed?

We want to protect patient safety while keeping the commercial model workable. We'll come back with a written counterproposal after legal review.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@acme-med.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA & Liability: request for severity-indexed buyout and remedies

Elliot / team —

Thanks for the redline and context. I reviewed Acme_Redlines_SLA_20270110.pdf and had an initial pass below. Our goal is to offer meaningful operational protections while keeping liability bounded so we can insure the program and continue to iterate on the service. High level counterpoints: 

- Buyout: Redwood is open to a limited, staged termination right tied to repeated, unremediated Severity 1 events. Proposed language: Acme may elect to terminate for convenience on 60 days' notice after the occurrence of two verified Severity 1 incidents within any rolling 12-month period, provided Redwood has failed to meet the remediation/cure obligations within the cure windows set out in Section X. Termination compensation would be pro-rated refund of pre-paid fees and a one-time wind-down fee up to 3x the average monthly committed fees (capped). This provides Acme an exit without leaving Redwood with open unlimited exposure.

- Fee-at-risk / LDs: we cannot accept uncapped, punitive liquidated damages tied to single incidents. We can offer a fee-at-risk schedule that escalates with repeat severity:
  * First verified Sev1: service credit + right to short-term remediation credit (no cash LD).
  * Second verified Sev1 within 12 months: a fee-at-risk payment equal to 2x monthly committed fees, held in escrow for 90 days pending remediation verification.
  * Third verified Sev1 within 12 months: termination right as above plus release of escrow to Acme.

- Latency: we can commit to p95 <= 200ms for the dedicated pool under normal operating load as defined in the performance annex. Missed p95 for 3 consecutive weekly reports would move the incident into a Severity 2 assessment and trigger the staged fee-at-risk (see annex). We need to define what constitutes a sustained platform-wide degradation vs. workload-specific anomalies.

- Auditability: we can provide signed daily summaries and an automated export of uptime/latency metrics to an S3 bucket with a signed manifest. Direct read access to internal telemetry is not feasible for security reasons, but we will provide attestations and signed CSV reports.

I've attached a proposed severity-index matrix (severity-index-matrix.xlsx) and inline redline suggestions in Acme_Redlines_SLA_20270110.pdf.

Please review and let us know whether the escrow/capped approach is a reasonable compromise. If Acme still requires uncapped LD or immediate unilateral buyout on first incident, we'll need to escalate to the execs to discuss underwriting and pricing impact.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@acme-med.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Acme Medical Systems Procurement <procurement@acme-med.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA & Liability: request for severity-indexed buyout and remedies

Marissa / Camila —

Appreciate the quick review. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The reason Acme asks for a more immediate buyout/LD on first major Sev1 is regulatory exposure. If patient alerts are missed or reporting windows are missed due to platform unavailability, Acme can be subject to fines and recalls. Waiting for a second event to trigger an exit leaves us exposed.

- We're open to a capped approach, but the cap needs to be large enough to cover likely regulatory fines + customer remediation costs. Please ask your risk/finance team for an example of the capped numbers you are willing to underwrite (e.g., 6x monthly commit or a fixed dollar cap).

- For telemetry: signed manifests + S3 export are acceptable as long as the manifest includes per-route p95 and incident markers.

If Redwood can share proposed numeric caps and an illustrative fee-at-risk schedule, that will make it easier for procurement to take an internal position. Otherwise we'll need to pause the pilot and continue evaluation with other vendors.

—Elliot
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@acme-med.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA & Liability: request for severity-indexed buyout and remedies

Elliot —

Thanks — understood on the regulatory impact. We want to keep Acme on Redwood and make this work. Quick summary of where Redwood is willing to land for an enterprise amendment (proposal):

- Immediate remedies: For a verified Severity 1 incident with clear regulatory impact as documented in the incident review, Redwood will place an amount equal to 3x the average committed monthly fees into escrow within 10 business days. That escrow will remain pending remediation verification for 90 days.

- Escrow / Buyout path: If the incident leads to regulatory action or material customer harm (as described in the incident report) and remediation is not successful within 90 days, Acme may elect to terminate for convenience with a pro-rated refund of prepaid fees plus release of escrow to Acme up to the capped amount (3x monthly commit).

- Repeat incidents: The second verified Severity 1 within 12 months increases escrow to 6x monthly commit and opens a 30-day cure window; third verified incident allows immediate termination and release of escrow.

- Latency: we commit to p95 <= 200ms under the dedicated pool performance annex. If missed for 3 consecutive weekly reports, we will treat that period as a Severity 2 incident subject to staged fee-at-risk described above.

- Telemetry: we'll provide the S3 export with per-route p95, daily signed manifests, and an incident packet for any Sev1 event.

Next steps: Chloe and Marissa will draft the amendment reflecting the capped-escrow approach and the example numeric caps (we'll show 3x and 6x as above, plus a fixed-dollar cap option). I can set a Thurs 10:00 AM PT exec call for final alignment (Camila, Marissa, Rishi, Elliot + Acme legal/procurement). If that works I'll send a calendar invite and attach the draft amendment and the DocuSign link for a non-binding term sheet.

Attaching: Acme_Redlines_SLA_20270110.pdf (redline with our edits), severity-index-matrix.xlsx (proposed severity definitions).

Best,
Camila
